summary: Neutral-pion suppression in oxygen collisions, equilibrium baselines for momentum correlations, parton-scale initial-state fluctuations, and generative simulation of TPC backgrounds.
strongest_paper_summary: ALICE oxygen double ratio and production-level TPC background simulation

papers.title: Nuclear Modification of π⁰ Production in pO and OO Collisions with ALICE
papers.abstract: The proceedings presents neutral-pion nuclear modification measurements in pO and OO collisions and compares the results with cold and hot nuclear matter calculations.
papers.summary: The double ratio R_OO/R_pO² is suppressed relative to a cold-matter baseline by 4.9 standard deviations. This is a proceedings account of the earlier ALICE result, not a new independent measurement.
papers.assessment: Strong experimental relevance, but the cancellation of cold-matter effects depends on the model and kinematic matching; the measurement does not distinguish energy-loss mechanisms.

papers.title: Accelerating ALICE Background Simulations: A WGAN-GP Approach to Slow-Neutron-Induced TPC Loopers
papers.abstract: A generative model replaces slow-neutron transport with generated electron and positron backgrounds for ALICE simulation, preserving key looper distributions and accelerating transport.
papers.summary: Integrated into ALICE O2 production for pp and Pb–Pb, the model reduces the tested transport time from 21.5 s to about 2.0 s per event.
papers.assessment: Strong practical use case with production deployment and full-simulation comparisons. The looper rate is normalized separately, momentum tails need improvement, and the speedup is for transport, not end-to-end processing.

papers.title: Equilibrium baseline for transverse-momentum correlations in Au+Au collisions at 3–39 GeV
papers.abstract: An equilibrium hadron-resonance-gas calculation includes decays, quantum statistics, collective flow and conservation laws in a baseline for transverse-momentum correlations.
papers.summary: The calculation underpredicts STAR correlations by factors of 3–4 in central collisions at 11.5–39 GeV and becomes negative at 3–5.2 GeV, where the data are positive.
papers.assessment: Useful explicit baseline and direct data comparison. The discrepancy does not establish a critical point: freeze-out assumptions, acceptance, and nonequilibrium and flow fluctuations matter.

papers.title: Introducing Parton-Level Fluctuations in the TRENTo-Sea Model
papers.abstract: TRENTo-Sea samples parton momentum fractions from nuclear PDFs and models parton-level interactions to study initial geometry and granularity.
papers.summary: The model reproduces eccentricity from calibrated models except in central collisions, and finds that low-x parton populations affect local geometry.
papers.assessment: Promising initial-state framework rather than direct validation against final-state measurements. The infrared regulator is calibrated to pp cross sections and central-collision disagreement remains.
